topic.title: the next room
topic.claim: Papa never tells you he's proud. He tells the neighbour, loudly, while you're in the next room.
topic.moment: You're inside and you hear papa through the wall, telling Sharma uncle exactly what you earn and where you work.

turn.believed: Papa doesn't say he's proud because he isn't the type, or isn't quite proud.
turn.actually: He's proud enough to broadcast it to the whole lane, just never to your face.

topic.because: Praising you directly might soften you, or break a lifetime of a certain kind of distance. The neighbour is how he says it where you can hear but he doesn't have to look at you.
topic.payoff: He wasn't hiding that he's proud. He was performing it, loud enough for you to overhear.
topic.feeling: the warmth of being loved sideways
topic.villain: the arrangement where a father's pride has to travel through a neighbour to reach his child
topic.behaviour: fathers brag about their kids to everyone except the kid
topic.mechanism: saying it to your face breaks the distance he's used to, so he routes the pride through someone you can overhear
topic.send_to: a friend whose dad has never once said it to them directly
topic.why_now: home visits this season when you overhear these conversations again
